title: Choose the visual world for Star Auction
question: The roll assigned Stadium Scoreboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Stadium Scoreboard
options.lineage: LED stadium scoreboards and the fourth official's substitution board
options.thesis: The auction runs on the stadium's own scoreboard: every lot, bid and second lit in LED you can read from the far end of the majlis.
options.viewport: Top half is the lit board: the lot in big type, the current bid in giant LED numerals and a game clock. Below sit the two team panels (home/away) with their budgets, and chunky bid buttons.
options.risk: Arabic dot-matrix faces are rare, so names stay in solid Arabic type and the LED treatment goes on numerals and labels. Done timidly, it reads as retro-arcade.

raised.raise: One dot grid sets the whole numeric type scale, with no free-floating font sizes.
Each panel owns one truth and shows its trend: budgets show the last delta, the clock shows its drain.
The squad builds as one lit course per round, a visible record of the draft.
One alert colour is reserved for the live lot and nothing else.

options.label: Match Night Broadcast
options.lineage: Arabic sports-TV graphics packages: score bug, lower thirds, deadline-day ticker
options.thesis: The auction is broadcast live, like transfer deadline night on Arabic sports TV.
options.viewport: A broadcast frame: the lot as an angled lower-third over the pitch, a score bug with both budgets, and a breaking ticker of past sales.
options.risk: This is the familiar choice: most sports apps already look like TV graphics.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: airport gate boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: The transfer window as a live departures board: each lot is a row that reranks and flashes when its status changes.
options.viewport: A board of the round's lots, plus your squad as a boarding pass with a segment per position.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (transfers are departures, and the change flash maps to a new top bid) and is strong on clarity, but Arab fans place football on the stadium board before the airport board.
options.risk: It can read as travel-app cosplay, and the hidden card has no natural home on a board.

options.label: Fight-Night Poster
options.lineage: Hatch Show Print letterpress wood-type posters
options.thesis: Every round is printed as tonight's bout poster: the lot in full-width wood-type bands, each new bid a fresh ink pass.
options.viewport: One tall broadside with the player's name filling the measure, the bid as a red overprint and the rivals billed below.
options.case: Strong headline clarity and the bid-as-ink-pass is memorable, but letterpress posters are not Arab football's own culture.
options.risk: Cream plus wood type drifts into a craft-fair look, and Arabic wood type is hard to source.

options.label: Phosphor Glyph Scene
options.thesis: The table drawn entirely in glyph density.
options.viewport: The lot rendered as a glyph portrait.
options.risk: Arabic doesn't fit a monospace grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: Arabic can't hold a monospace glyph grid, and fans don't recognise it.
options.kept: One strict grid sets the type scale.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Bid, clock and budgets as cockpit gauges.
options.risk: Reads as a tool, not a game night.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a cockpit is a tool costume with no football in it.
options.kept: Each panel owns one truth and shows its trend.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: The squad rises course by course.
options.risk: Slow and earthy where the game is fast.
options.case: Fuses poorly: earth and slowness work against a timed bidding war.
options.kept: The draft as a visible, course-by-course build record.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.thesis: Each lot as a film frame.
options.viewport: A film strip of the rounds.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the grain fights readability at arm's length.
options.kept: One alert colour reserved for the live lot only.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The football-card game look: gold and silver rated cards on a dark pitch-green field.
canonCard.viewport: A big glowing player card in the centre, with budgets and bid buttons around it.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every football card game by design.
